Subject: Re: selective greylisting based on user preference

Dennis Trabjerg wrote:
>
> -Implemented /etc/postfix/per_recipient_greylist.cf with the following;
> hosts = my.mysql.server
> user = postfix_mysql_username
> password = postfix_mysql_password
> dbname = postfix_database
> table = postfix_usernames
> select_field = policy_service
> where_field = email_address

if your postfix isn't too old, better move to the "modern" syntax:

hosts = ...
user= ...
password = ..
dbname = ...
query = select policy_service from postfix_usernames where email_address
= '%s'

>
> -Modified my postfix_usernames table to contain a column 
> "policy_service" containing either "check_service" to enable 
> greylisting or "OK" to bypass greylisting.
>
> -Added a restriction class called "check_greylist"
> smtpd_restriction_classes = check_greylist
> check_greylist = check_policy_service inet:127.0.0.1:60000
>
> And added per_recipient_greylist.cf to my recipient restrictions. in 
> main.cf
>
> Now im just wondering what will happen if the MySQL query returns 
> something else than OK or check_greylist ?

if it returns a valid action (such as REJECT), then it will be used.
whether you want this (to implemenbt REJECT,/DISCARD/... for some
recipients) or not is up to you. if you want to guard against this, then add
    AND policy_service IN ('check_greylist', 'OK')
to the query.

>
> Also curious to try this approach with user-preference-based 
> amavisd-new and policy-d services. -Any comments on that issue ?

it would be possible to have a "common" design that merges all
preferences. but I've never worked on this.
>
> For now i have only implemented this solution on a low-volume 
> backup-mx, and tailing the logs at the moment. any concers on using 
> the above setup in a production enviroment ?

as far as your mysql server runs well, I see no problem. don't forget to
use proxymap to minimize the number of mysql connections.
